text:
Alex: Heads-up — after the kernel-selection change yesterday we see p99 latency for streamed small-kernel requests jump from ~120ms to ~210ms on nvlink hosts. Anyone else?
Maria: Yep saw it in the nightly perf dash. The change favored medium kernels for overall throughput; streaming microbatches now hit an extra kernel handoff.
Jin: Could be batch formation timing. If coalesce window grows slightly we accidentally force a kernel variant that has worse partial-decode warmup.
Maria: Quick numbers from profiler: tail of step_decode increased CPU spin by ~40% and kernel switch overhead added ~60us per request on average. KV cache hit rates unchanged.
Alex: Important detail: this regressed only when streaming is enabled + continuous batching. Non-streamed generation is fine.
Jin: Theory: continuous-batching heuristics choose to coalesce into a larger batch which triggers medium-kernel selection because of estimated seq_len distribution. For streaming we want earlier send even if batch is smaller.
Anna: SLOs: streaming p99 must be <180ms. We're above that now, so need mitigation before tomorrow's customer run.
Maria: Quick mitigation: reduce coalesce_window_ms for streaming route and bias eligibility to prefer small-kernel paths. Did a local A/B: coalesce 6ms vs 12ms -> p99 140ms vs 205ms.
Jin: Proposed config to test in canary (applies only to routes with streaming:true):
```
"batching": {
  "coalesce_window_ms": 6,
  "eligibility_tokens": 4,
  "token_budget_target": 16,
  "prefer_small_kernel_weight": 0.8
}
"partial_decode": {
  "schedule_threshold_ms": 2
}
```
Alex: Nice. Also add a safeguard to avoid oscillation: only apply prefer_small_kernel when avg_queue_depth < 8 for 1s.
Maria: I ran a perf job on canary-2: before change: p99 202ms, after tweak: p99 147ms, p50 unchanged. CPU overhead dropped ~25%. KV cache behavior stable.
runtime-bot: CI perf job #4587 completed — streaming route canary-2 metrics: p50: 34ms, p95: 78ms, p99: 149ms. Link: https://ci.internal/perf/4587
Jin: Good signal. Next step: implement rollout flag gated by route metadata and add metric to detect kernel handoff frequency.
Anna: +1 on rollout gate. Let's schedule a 2-hour canary this afternoon, rollback plan ready. Who will own?
Alex: I'll own deployment and monitor SLOs. Maria will push the heuristic toggle. Jin will add handoff metric and the no-oscillation guard.
Maria: Pushed PR with toggle and default smaller coalesce for streaming routes. Requesting review: https://phab/internal/D1234
Jin: I'll add the instrumentation and a short eval script to replay streaming traces with the new policy.
Alex: Thanks. If this fixes the perf without harming throughput too much we keep it. If throughput drops >5% across medium workloads we need a fallback to previous kernel policy during high load. :thumbsup:
